qs.q: Which clinical presentation is characteristic of a Pancoast tumour?
o: Horner syndrome and ulnar nerve pain
qs.e: Pancoast tumours are apical neoplasms that invade the brachial or cervical sympathetic plexus, causing Horner syndrome and pain in the ulnar nerve distribution. SVC syndrome results from mediastinal compression, not apical invasion.
